title.es: La jerga que de verdad oirás

es: Reconocer jerga y registro coloquial frecuentes (swamped, knackered, gutted, chuffed…), su equivalente neutro y el contexto en que suenan naturales o fuera de lugar.

teaching.en: A colleague might say she is swamped, but in a report to a client you would write that she is fully booked.
teaching.es: Una compañera puede decir que está desbordada, pero en un informe para un cliente escribirías que tiene la agenda completa.
teaching.explanationEs: Swamped es coloquial; el equivalente neutro es very busy o fully booked.
segments: A colleague might say she is swamped, but in a report
to a client you would write that she is fully booked.
teaching.audioText: A colleague might say she is swamped, but in a report to a client you would write that she is fully booked.

teaching.en: After a long flight, Leo says he is beat, while his British cousin, who is completely knackered, agrees.
teaching.es: Después de un vuelo largo, Leo dice que está hecho polvo, y su primo británico, que está completamente reventado, le da la razón.
teaching.explanationEs: Beat es más americano y knackered más británico; los dos significan muy cansado.
segments: After a long flight, Leo says he is beat,
while his British cousin, who is completely knackered, agrees.
teaching.audioText: After a long flight, Leo says he is beat, while his British cousin, who is completely knackered, agrees.

teaching.en: When your team loses, a friend might say bummer, but someone feeling gutted will usually say that he is very disappointed.
teaching.es: Cuando pierde tu equipo, un amigo puede decir «qué fastidio», pero quien se siente destrozado dirá normalmente que está muy decepcionado.
teaching.explanationEs: Bummer es una exclamación breve; gutted expresa una decepción fuerte y suena británico.
segments: When your team loses, a friend might say bummer, but someone
feeling gutted will usually say that he is very disappointed.
teaching.audioText: When your team loses, a friend might say bummer, but someone feeling gutted will usually say that he is very disappointed.

teaching.en: Let's chill or hang out sounds natural among friends, but in a job interview it could make you come across as careless.
teaching.es: «Let's chill» o «hang out» suena natural entre amigos, pero en una entrevista de trabajo podría hacerte parecer descuidado.
teaching.explanationEs: Come across as + adjetivo: la impresión que das. El registro elegido cambia esa impresión.
segments: Let's chill or hang out sounds natural among friends, but in
a job interview it could make you come across as careless.
teaching.audioText: Let's chill or hang out sounds natural among friends, but in a job interview it could make you come across as careless.

teaching.en: Awesome and no worries are friendly in a text message, but an apology to a client deserves something more formal.
teaching.es: Awesome y no worries resultan cordiales en un mensaje de texto, pero una disculpa a un cliente merece algo más formal.
teaching.explanationEs: Awesome sustituye a excellent; no worries a that is quite all right. Ambos son informales.
segments: Awesome and no worries are friendly in a text message,
but an apology to a client deserves something more formal.
teaching.audioText: Awesome and no worries are friendly in a text message, but an apology to a client deserves something more formal.

teaching.en: A British mate might say he is chuffed about his promotion, while an American friend would say he is thrilled.
teaching.es: Un amigo británico podría decir que está muy contento con su ascenso, mientras que uno estadounidense diría que está emocionado.
teaching.explanationEs: Chuffed es muy británico; mate, en la misma línea, se usa entre amigos.

prompt.es: ¿Qué mensaje dice lo mismo en registro neutro?

choices.text: I am very happy and relaxed, so I cannot come tonight; could we meet on Saturday?
I am very busy and exhausted, so I cannot come tonight; could we meet on Saturday?
I am very busy and angry, so I cannot come tonight; could we meet on Saturday?

feedback.es: Swamped equivale a very busy y knackered a exhausted; las otras opciones cambian el estado de ánimo del hablante.

hint.es: Traduce cada palabra coloquial por su equivalente neutro.

origin.text: Sorry mate, I'm swamped at work and completely knackered, so I'm going to skip tonight. Bummer, I know! Let's hang out on Saturday instead.

feedback.es: Gutted es la palabra británica para una decepción fuerte.

origin.text: Mia failed the exam by two points. She was absolutely ___ about it, because she had hoped to pass with a good mark.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Awesome queda bien en un mensaje, pero no en un informe.»

answer.text: Awesome is fine in a text but not in a report

feedback.es: El registro decide dónde cabe la palabra: un mensaje entre amigos sí, un informe no.

hint.es: Primero la palabra coloquial, y al final el contraste con not in a report.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué prefiere hacer Tom esa noche.

choices.text: Go out and celebrate getting the job.
Catch up on work he has fallen behind with.
Stay in and rest after his night shift.

feedback.es: Tom está agotado tras el turno de noche y prefiere relajarse en casa; la buena noticia del empleo llega después, y nadie habla de trabajo atrasado.

origin.audio: I met Tom at the station. He said he was completely knackered after the night shift, and that he would rather chill at home than go out. I said no worries, mate, and we left it there. Then he texted me: awesome news, he is chuffed, because he has got the job.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión coloquial con su significado.

feedback.es: Las cuatro expresiones se oyen entre amigos: decepción, alegría, planes informales y quitar importancia.

prompt.es: ¿Qué mensaje es adecuado para declinar una entrevista de trabajo?

choices.text: I am afraid I cannot attend on Tuesday, as I am fully booked that day.
Sorry mate, I'm swamped on Tuesday, so I'll skip it, no worries!
Bummer, but I'm knackered on Tuesday, so can we chill about it?

feedback.es: A un empleador se le escribe en registro neutro; las otras dos mezclan jerga de amigos y dan mala impresión.

origin.text: You are writing to the manager of a company to say that you cannot attend Tuesday's interview. Which message is best?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la hablante sobre su nueva compañera de apartamento.

choices.text: She thinks her flatmate is rude to the landlord.
She likes her, but finds her energy tiring.
She would like to move out because of her flatmate's plans.

feedback.es: Elogia a su compañera, pero el humor final (seguir hablando a través de la puerta) revela que su energía la cansa.

origin.audio: My new flatmate is a lovely girl, really, and a proper laugh. She is chuffed to bits with the flat, and she calls everyone mate, even the landlord. But she does come across as a bit much at seven in the morning. Last Sunday I was knackered, and she wanted to hang out and plan the whole week. I said no worries, I'll just lie down for ten minutes. Honestly, I am not complaining; I am only saying that some people are not ready for a whole week of plans before breakfast. Half an hour later, she was still talking to me through the door.

prompt.es: ¿Qué impresión probable causa este correo en el cliente?

choices.text: That the sender is concealing the true reason for the delay.
That the sender has too much work and expects the client to help.
That the sender treats the client and the delay too lightly.

feedback.es: El retraso se explica, pero el registro de amigos hace que el cliente pueda sentir que se le toma poco en serio; la razón no se oculta ni se le pide ayuda.

origin.text: Hi Mr Hughes, sorry mate, the report is going to be late. I'm completely swamped this week, and I'm knackered, to be honest. Bummer, I know! No worries if you're annoyed, we can hang out on Friday and sort it out. I'll send you everything as soon as I can, I promise, and I'll bring the coffee.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tras tres semanas de resfriado, estaba agotadísimo y durmió doce horas.»

feedback.es: Knackered es el coloquial británico para agotado; beat es la variante más americana.

origin.text: After three weeks of a bad cold, he was absolutely ___ and slept for twelve hours without a break.

prompt.es: Reescribe el mensaje en registro neutro para un cliente.

answer.text: I am very busy this week and extremely tired, so I am afraid I cannot attend on Thursday. I apologise for that. Could we meet on Saturday instead?
accepted: I am very busy this week and extremely tired, so I am afraid I cannot attend on Thursday. I apologise for that. Could we meet on Saturday instead?
I am fully booked this week and exhausted, so unfortunately I cannot come on Thursday. I am sorry about that. Would Saturday suit you instead?

feedback.es: El registro neutro sustituye swamped y knackered por equivalentes formales y convierte el plan en una propuesta educada.

origin.text: Hey mate, I'm swamped this week and completely knackered, so I'll skip Thursday. Bummer, I know! Let's hang out on Saturday instead, no worries?

prompt.es: ¿Qué busca el autor con este mensaje a un amigo?

choices.text: To decline this invitation kindly while showing he still wants to meet.
To ask his friend to change the date because his gran is ill.
To excuse himself from the group because he is too tired to go out.

feedback.es: Rechaza esa fecha con una razón y propone alternativas y comida: declina con amabilidad y mantiene la relación; no pide cambiar la fecha por enfermedad ni se aparta del grupo.

origin.text: Thanks for the invite! I'd love to hang out, but I've promised my gran a visit, and then I'll probably be knackered. No worries if the plan changes, though: I'm up for a chill evening any time next week, and I'll bring the snacks. Say hi to everybody from me, and tell them that I am thinking of them.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esa palabra parecería demasiado informal para un cliente.»

answer.text: That word would come across as too casual for a client

feedback.es: Come across as + adjetivo describe la impresión que causa una palabra en un contexto formal.

prompt.es: Completa: «No pasa nada, amigo; le podría pasar a cualquiera.»

feedback.es: No worries es la respuesta habitual, cordial e informal, a una disculpa.

origin.text: Sorry about the mix-up, it was entirely my fault. No ___, mate; it could have happened to anyone.
